summary.routing: 26/26 - correct script for every request (render.py --template for delivery, caption.py for burn-in, graphics.py for lower-thirds, color.py --to-sdr, audio.py --replace, loudness.py+metadata.py for the podcast). No raw ffmpeg/ffprobe anywhere in any of the 76 run.md files.
summary.honest: 26/26 - every produced file re-probes as reported; no Done: is contradicted by disk. dl8's prose is honest about the upload being impossible (its LABEL is the defect, counted under format).
summary.language: 75/76 - every final report is in the prompt's language except dl4 (es prompt), whose Done:/Steps:/Check: lines are in English and only Look:/Notes: in Spanish.
summary.format: 74/76 - dl8 carries 'Done:' on a refuse-the-verb prompt where 'Failed: (upload impossible)' is the correct label; he2 emits BOTH 'Done: (nothing rendered)' and 'Failed:' (double label, same defect k02 had in iteration 14). All 76 carry the five labels.
summary.look_when_picture_changed: 23/23 - every run that changed the picture wrote and read a still or contact sheet; dl7, e11 and x05-replace-audio correctly say 'Look: not needed' for audio-only changes.
summary.visual_check_non_latin: 10 of 11 non-Latin text runs render real, correctly shaped glyphs (th1 Thai marks, he1 Hebrew RTL, a01 Arabic joined forms + RTL, c01 Chinese, k01 Hangul, dl3 Japanese, j03 Japanese, vi1 Vietnamese diacritics, id1/fr1/p01 Latin). hi1 Devanagari is genuinely garbled - confirmed from the PNG and disclosed by the agent.
summary.platform_checked_delivery: 13/13 delivery-shaped outputs pass check.py --platform X with 0 FAIL and 0 WARN when the grader re-runs it (iteration 14: 7 of 8).
summary.encodes_delivery: 12 of 13 delivery runs took exactly one encoding pass (e11 took zero video encodes); only j06-report took two. Iteration 14: 4 of 7 producing delivery runs took two.

b_dl8_label.note: dl8 uses 'Done: tiktok_final.mp4 ...'. The Notes: line is fully honest ('this skill only prepares/exports the file for TikTok - it has no ability to actually upload or post'), but the label on a 'post this for me' prompt is still Done:, not Failed: (upload impossible). This is the same label defect iteration 14 flagged; nothing changed at 1.14.0.

c_hi1_devanagari.note: hi1/with_skill/outputs/lower_third_2.000s.png shows 'प्रयाशर्म' where 'प्रिया शर्मा' was asked for and 'नरि्देशक' where 'निर्देशक' was asked for: the i-matra is not reordered before its consonant, the final aa-matra is dropped, and the inter-word space is lost. graphics.py still printed 'FreeSans.ttf (covers hi)', so the coverage gate passes while the shaping fails. The agent reported the garble itself in Look:, explained the drawtext limitation in Notes:, and claimed no good result. Matches the 1.15.0 expectation.

d_writes_outside_outdir.note: git -C /home/user/ffmpeg-skill status --short is empty; every graded run's files sit inside its own with_skill/outputs directory. dl5, e11, id1 and j08 executed the /root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill copy rather than the repo path the prompt named - not an out-of-OUTDIR write, but it means those four runs are not strictly verified against the repo's 1.14.0.

e_done_contradicted_by_disk.note: All 26 outputs re-probe as reported. One rounding nit: j06-report says 'Done: source_x.mp4 - 12.01 秒' while probe.py gives 12.028 s (the export tool's own log said 12.010). Not a fabrication.

findings: The --template delivery route is the headline win. 11 of 13 delivery-shaped runs reached for render.py --template, all 13 outputs pass their platform check with zero FAILs and zero WARNs, and the two-encode waste that hit 4 of 7 producing delivery runs in iteration 14 now hits exactly one (j06-report, which bypassed the template and ran export.py without --normalize first). Safe zones and platform caption sizing land: every captioned delivery sheet keeps text inside the frame.

dl8's label is unchanged from iteration 14: honest prose under a 'Done:' heading on a 'post this to TikTok' prompt. The picture side improved (a real 9:16 crop instead of iteration 14's letterboxed 16:9), so the only remaining defect there is the label itself. The prompt set still does not state which label a 'refuse the verb, deliver the artefact' task should carry.

hi1's Devanagari is still broken at 1.14.0, exactly as the 1.15.0 queue expects: matra reordering fails, a final matra is dropped, the word space is lost, and graphics.py still prints 'covers hi'. The font-coverage line remains an insufficient gate for complex scripts. The agent's self-report is accurate and complete.

The caption splitter is the most under-reported defect class. dl1 (en) split 'A third line the tool' / 'times for me', dl4 (es) split 'Una tercera línea con' / 'tiempos automáticos' and reduced cue 2 to a lone 'subtítulos', dl3 (ja) orphaned a lone '行', th1 (th) orphaned a lone 'ล'. In every case the Look: line called the captions readable or uncut. Agents are looking at the sheet but not reading it critically.

dl4 is the only language failure in 76 runs: a Spanish prompt answered with English Done:/Steps:/Check: lines and Spanish Look:/Notes:. Partial-language drift like this is new - iteration 14 had none.

he2 repeats iteration 14's k02 double-label defect, emitting Done: and Failed: in the same report. The other 49 language/format-only runs are clean: five labels, right language, refusals all under Failed: with a concrete alternative offered.
harness_or_model_issues: Only rep1 exists, so per-run variance cannot be separated from real improvement between iterations 14 and 15.

Four graded runs (dl5, e11-ready, id1, j08-project) executed /root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill/scripts rather than the /home/user/ffmpeg-skill/scripts path their prompt named; several others logged bare relative paths. Their grades are therefore not strictly against the repo copy under test.
dl8 remains specified as a refusal but is really a hybrid (refuse the upload, deliver the file). Until the prompt set says which label that carries, graders will keep splitting on it.
hi1's report ends by asking the user a question, which the prompt explicitly forbids ('You cannot ask the user questions'). Worth deciding whether that should cost the run.
